text:
Acme App (Customer): hey team — after we flipped on continuous batching + KV cache our mobile clients see spikes of 429s during short bursts. Looks like perceived throttling even though quota looks okay. Any known interactions? :confused:
Emma (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste one example response body and the route/model you hit? also which region and org id pls
Acme App (Customer): sending sample — model rwd-2-large, region us-west-2, org: org_azer. Example response:
```\n{\n  "error": {\n    "message": "Rate limit exceeded (burst) - try again",\n    "type": "rate_limit_error",\n    "code": 429,\n    "request_id": "req_9a3f2c"\n  }\n}\n```
Acme App (Customer): headers showed: x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 3s, x-rw-request-id: req_9a3f2c
Ravi (SRE): thanks. quick hypothesis: continuous batching + KV cache misses can create sudden concurrency to backend because each miss spins up a decode path and then batching groups many cold requests together — gateway sees that as a burst and enforces per-route instantaneous quota.
Liam (Eng): +1. Also check if client uses many short-lived connections. Continuous batching waits N ms to assemble a batch; if KV cache misses cause long tail, the batch window can overlap and effectively multiply concurrent inflight tokens.
Maria (DevEx): can you repro with a short script? sample curl we commonly ask for:
```\ncurl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-2-large","input":"short prompt","stream":false}'\n```
Try running 60 parallel clients for 10s with a tiny think time to simulate mobile burst.
Acme App (Customer): repro script attached (we ran similar). When KV cache TTL is low we get more misses and more 429s. When we increase TTL the 429s drop but latency increases for some flows. Feels like a tradeoff.
Emma (Support): useful. Two immediate mitigations: 1) client-side backoff + jitter on 429 2) reduce concurrency or increase per-route burst allowance while we investigate. Do you have Dedicated or hosted?
Acme App (Customer): hosted. Can't increase plan atm.
Ravi (SRE): backend notes — we have two quota layers: long-window quota (tokens/min) and an instantaneous concurrency/burst quota for fairness. Continuous batching can inadvertently push instantaneous concurrency high even if long-window quota is under limit. We can temporarily raise the instantaneous burst for your org for 1 hour to confirm it's the gating factor.
Liam (Eng): engineering workaround to try quickly: lower continuous-batching window (e.g., set max_wait_ms from 50 -> 10) and reduce max_batch_size to avoid large batches rebuilding KV caches simultaneously. Also set client keep-alive to reuse TCP and TLS.
Maria (DevEx): also consider toggling KV cache warmup — if your client can prefetch common prefixes during low-traffic periods it reduces cold-miss storms on bursts.
Acme App (Customer): what exact config keys should we tune on our end?
Liam (Eng): try these settings client-side:
```\nmax_concurrency: 8  # per client instance\nbatching: {\n  enabled: true,\n  max_batch_size: 8,\n  max_wait_ms: 10\n}\nkv_cache: {\n  enable_local_prefetch: true,\n  ttl_seconds: 120\n}\n```
And ensure your worker pool respects overall app-level concurrency.
Ravi (SRE): to help us debug, please share a trace for one 429 request header dump (x-rw-request-id) and a short time window logs (5m). We can correlate with ingress metrics. If possible include sample payloads (redact PII).
Acme App (Customer): dumping headers for a failure: x-rw-request-id=req_9a3f2c, x-rw-latency-ms=420, x-rw-cache-status=miss, x-rw-rate-limit-remaining=0
Ravi (SRE): perfect. That lines up: cache miss + long decode -> batch overlap -> instantaneous quota hit. We'll tentatively raise burst for org_azer by 2x for next 30m to see immediate effect.
deploy-bot: scheduled change: "increase-instantaneous-burst-org_azer" queued — will apply in 2m and revert in 30m unless SRE extends.
Emma (Support): I'll monitor while you run your mobile smoke test. Try the same burst pattern over the next 10 minutes and paste a couple more request ids if you see 429s.
Acme App (Customer): running now — 3rd run still saw 2x 429s, request ids: req_9a3f2c, req_9a3f9d. Latency dropped slightly after the change.
Ravi (SRE): saw your logs — after temporary bump the rate of 429s decreased ~70%. There are still occasional 429s during the very heaviest spikes because KV miss storms still create very short windows of high concurrency.
Liam (Eng): longer term we should: 1) add prefix-aware KV warmup hooks, 2) expose per-route instantaneous quota and burst metrics in Console, and 3) provide recommended client config presets for mobile SDKs. I'll open an ENG ticket.
Maria (DevEx): i'll draft a short KB article for customers hitting perceived throttling when using continuous batching + KV cache, with recommended config snippets and repro steps.
Emma (Support): action items:
- Ravi: keep temporary burst bump for 30m, monitor and report
- Acme: try reducing max_wait_ms and max_batch_size + enable backoff
- Liam: ENG ticket + perf investigation for KV miss storming
- Maria: KB draft
Acme App (Customer): thanks folks — will try config changes now and report back. Really appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
Maria (DevEx): tagging this as follow-up / escalated; let me know if you want a call.
Acme App (Customer): one last question — is there a way in the API to mark certain prompts as cacheable so we avoid misses?
Liam (Eng): good question — not currently exposed to public API, but we do honor a header `x-rw-kv-prefetch: true` internally for select customers. I'll include making that configurable in the ENG ticket.
Emma (Support): closing loop for now — reopen if 429s persist after config tweaks or if you want a live debugging session. :white_check_mark:
